c)

```{r}

model_1R <- glm(AUAREQC ~ RIAGENDR, family = poisson(link = "log"), data = data)
model_2R <- glm(AUAREQC ~ RIAGENDR + factor(DMDCITZN) + DMDHHSZA + INDHHIN2, family = poisson(link = "log"), data = data)

model_1L <- glm(AUALEQC ~ RIAGENDR, family = poisson(link = "log"), data = data)
model_2L <- glm(AUAREQC ~ RIAGENDR + factor(DMDCITZN) + DMDHHSZA + INDHHIN2, family = poisson(link = "log"), data = data)

```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(broom)
library(knitr)

# 1. Put your models into a named list
models <- list(
  "Model 1R" = model_1R, 
  "Model 2R" = model_2R, 
  "Model 1L" = model_1L, 
  "Model 2L" = model_2L
)

# 2. Extract and format coefficients (IRRs) for all models
coef_part <- map_dfr(models, ~ tidy(.x, exponentiate = TRUE), .id = "Model") %>%
  mutate(
    # Add significance stars to the IRR values
    stars = case_when(
      p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE            ~ ""
    ),
    IRR_Label = paste0(round(estimate, 3), stars)
  ) %>%
  select(Model, term, IRR_Label) %>%
  # Pivot into a wide format where each model gets its own column
  pivot_wider(names_from = Model, values_from = IRR_Label, values_fill = "-") %>%
  rename(Statistic = term)

# 3. Extract model diagnostics (N, AIC, Pseudo-R2)
stats_part <- map_dfr(models, function(m) {
  pseudo_r2 <- 1 - (logLik(m) / logLik(update(m, . ~ 1)))
  data.frame(
    N = as.character(nobs(m)),
    AIC = as.character(round(AIC(m), 3)),
    `Pseudo R²` = as.character(round(pseudo_r2, 3)),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}, .id = "Model") %>%
  # Pivot long and wide to align with the coefficients layout
  pivot_longer(-Model, names_to = "Statistic", values_to = "Value") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Model, values_from = Value)

# 4. Combine coefficients and stats into a single final table
final_table <- bind_rows(coef_part, stats_part)

# 5. Output as a clean HTML table using kable
kable(final_table, 
      format = "html", 
      align = "lcccc",
      caption = "Poisson Regression Results: Incidence Risk Ratios (IRRs) and Model Statistics")


```

d)
```{r}
summary(model_2L)
library(marginaleffects)
avg_predictions(model_2L, variables = "RIAGENDR")
```
We therefore conclude that males have a bigger predicted risk ratio. It is statistically significant.
# Exercise 2

a)

```{r}
library(DBI) 
library(dplyr)

db <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "sakila_master.db")

#1)

v1 <- function() {
results <- dbGetQuery(db, "
    SELECT store.store_id, customer_list.notes
    FROM store 
    JOIN customer_list ON store.store_id = customer_list.SID 
    JOIN customer ON customer.customer_id = customer_list.ID
  ")
  
  total <- results %>% 
    group_by(store_id) %>% 
    summarise(total_customers = n(),
              average_active = mean(notes == "active", na.rm = TRUE),.groups = "drop")
  
  return(total)

}


#2)

v2 <- function() {
results <- dbGetQuery(db, "SELECT AVG( CASE WHEN customer_list.notes = 'active' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) AS average_active, COUNT(customer_list.ID) AS total FROM store JOIN customer_list on store.store_id = customer_list.SID JOIN customer on customer.customer_id = customer_list.ID GROUP BY store.store_id")
print(results)
}


```

pattern <- "@([^@]+)$"

match_rows <- regexpr(pattern, data$email, perl = TRUE)
domains <- regmatches(data$email, match_rows)

domains <- gsub("@", "", domains)

d)

```{r}
library(stringr)

# Function to clean and format into cell phone style (1234-567-890)
format_to_cell <- function(phone_col) {
  # 1. Remove all non-digits
  clean_digits <- str_replace_all(phone_col, "\\D", "")
  # 2. Reformat using regex capture groups
  str_replace(clean_digits, "(\\d{4})(\\d{3})(\\d{3})", "\\1-\\2-\\3")
}

# Apply to your columns
data$phone1 <- format_to_cell(data$phone1)
data$phone2 <- format_to_cell(data$phone2)

# Print the first 10 rows of each column to verify
head(data[, c("phone1", "phone2")], 10)
```

```{r}
pattern <- "(?i)(apt|apartment|unit|#)\\s*([a-z0-9-]+)"

df <- data %>% 
  mutate(apt_full = str_extract(address, pattern))

df <- df %>% 
  mutate(
    apt_cleaned = as.integer(str_remove(apt_full, "#"))
  )

print(df)

hist(log(df$apt_cleaned), na.rm = TRUE)
```

f)
```{r}
pattern <- "(?i)(apt|apartment|unit|#)\\s*([a-z0-9-]+)"

df <- data %>% 
  mutate(apt_full = str_extract(address, pattern))

df <- df %>% 
  mutate(
    apt_cleaned = as.integer(substr(str_remove(apt_full, "#"), 1, 1))
  )

print(df)

hist(df$apt_cleaned, na.rm = TRUE)
```

Yes, we see 1 is the most common - so it is followed.
